supplier61_checks.quote: If [[alg-uniform-interval-linear-residual-certifier]] returns `certified` with $(R,\widehat x,q,r)$, then every $(A,b)$ in the admitted families has a unique solution and its distance from $\widehat x$ is at most $r/(1-q)$. Inconclusive output asserts no such conclusion.

Input $n\ge1$, a nonempty family of Hermitian $n\times n$ matrices enclosed by complex rectangles, a point matrix $V\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, a real diagonal matrix $\Theta\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and proposed nonnegative bounds $\delta,\rho,M_A,M_\Theta,\tau$. Treat point data as exact dyadics and the family as any subset of its enclosure.

1. With outward interval evaluation, enclose $V^*V-I$ and every $AV-V\Theta$ for the full family. Form Frobenius upper bounds $d,r$ for these two matrices. Also form Frobenius upper bounds $m_A$ for every $A$ in the family and $m_\Theta$ for $\Theta$. If any enclosure or square-root operation is non-finite, return `inconclusive`.

2. Verify by outward scalar comparisons that $d\le\delta<1$, $r\le\rho$, $m_A\le M_A$, $m_\Theta\le M_\Theta$, and that $1-\sqrt{1-\delta}\le\tau$. If any comparison is undecided or false, return `inconclusive` with the failed check. Otherwise outward-compute a finite upper bound $\bar\eta\ge\rho+(M_A+M_\Theta)\tau$. For each increasingly sorted diagonal entry $\theta_{(k)}$, outward-compute finite endpoints $\ell_k\le\theta_{(k)}-\bar\eta$ and $u_k\ge\theta_{(k)}+\bar\eta$, and set $I_k=[\ell_k,u_k]$. If the radius bound or any final endpoint cannot be enclosed finitely, return `inconclusive`; otherwise return `certified` with radius bound $\bar\eta$ and intervals $I_1,\ldots,I_n$.

The checks use the Frobenius norm as an upper bound for the operator 2-norm. An inconclusive check makes no statement about the true spectrum.

If [[alg-near-orthonormal-hermitian-eigenvalue-certifier]] returns `certified` with outward radius bound $\bar\eta$ and intervals $I_k$, then for every admitted Hermitian $A$ its $k$-th increasing eigenvalue lies in $I_k$. Each $I_k$ contains the symmetric interval $[\theta_{(k)}-\bar\eta,\theta_{(k)}+\bar\eta]$. Inconclusive output makes no spectral claim.
